column1: comprehensive§A comprehensive index doubles the useful life of a book.§一份**完备**的索引能让一本书的使用寿命翻倍。
compromise§A leak compromised the whole set of negotiations.§一次泄密**危及**了整轮谈判。
compulsive§The book is compulsive reading and very badly organized.§这本书**让人放不下**，结构却糟糕透顶。
compunction§He felt some compunction about quoting a private letter.§引用一封私人信件让他有些**良心不安**。
conceal§Concealing a defect is worse in law than causing one.§在法律上，**隐瞒**缺陷比造成缺陷更严重。
concealment§Concealment turned a small error into a resignation.§**隐瞒**把一个小错误变成了一次辞职。
concede§I concede the point and dispute what follows from it.§我**承认**这一点，但不同意由此得出的推论。
conceivable§It is barely conceivable that both dates are right.§两个日期都对，这几乎**难以想象**。
concentration§The concentration of salt rises through the summer.§盐的**浓度**在整个夏天不断上升。
concession§The concession to run the ferry lasted ninety-nine years.§经营渡轮的**特许**权持续了九十九年。
conciliatory§A conciliatory gesture costs nothing and settles most disputes.§一个**安抚**性的姿态不花什么，却能了结多数争端。
concise§Be concise in the summary and thorough in the appendix.§摘要要**简洁**，附录要详尽。
conclusive§Only the third test was conclusive.§只有第三次检验才是**决定性**的。
concoct§The chemist concocted a dye from two waste products.§这位化学家用两种废料**调配**出一种染料。
concordance§A concordance of the poems runs to six hundred pages.§这些诗的**用语索引**长达六百页。
concordant§Two concordant witnesses are worth more than ten vague ones.§两个说法**一致**的证人胜过十个含糊的。
concur§I concur with the finding and not with the remedy.§我**同意**这个结论，但不同意这个补救办法。
condemnation§Condemnation of the building preceded its collapse by a week.§这栋楼被**判定危房**一周后就塌了。
condemnatory§A condemnatory report was filed and then lost.§一份**谴责性**的报告被归档，随后就丢了。
condense§Steam condenses on the cold pipe and drips all night.§蒸汽在冷管上**凝结**，整夜滴水。
condescend§He would not condescend to explain, which ended his career.§他不肯**屈尊**解释，这断送了他的职业生涯。
conditional§Approval was conditional and everyone read it as final.§批准是**有条件的**，所有人却都当作最终决定。
condone§Silence from the top was read as condoning the practice.§高层的沉默被理解为**默许**这种做法。
confer§The two editors conferred for an hour and changed one word.§两位编辑**商议**了一小时，改了一个词。
confession§A confession made under pressure is worth very little.§在压力下作出的**供认**价值很低。
confident§Be confident about the method and humble about the result.§对方法要**有信心**，对结果要谦虚。
configuration§The configuration of the valley funnels every storm through the town.§这个山谷的**地形**把每一场风暴都灌进镇子。
confine§Confine your comments to the section under discussion.§请把意见**限定**在正在讨论的这一节。
conflagration§The conflagration of 1666 reshaped the whole city.§一六六六年的**大火**重塑了整座城市。
conflate§Do not conflate cause with occasion.§不要把原因与时机**混为一谈**。
conformist§A conformist age produces conformist buildings.§**循规蹈矩**的时代造出循规蹈矩的建筑。
conformity§Conformity of style across forty authors took two editors.§让四十位作者的**文体统一**，用了两位编辑。
confound§Late frost confounds every planting calendar in the region.§晚霜**打乱**了这个地区所有的播种历。
confusion§There is a confusion here between two men of the same name.§这里把两个同名的人**搞混**了。
congenial§The climate is congenial to olives and hostile to apples.§这里的气候**宜于**橄榄，却不利于苹果。
conjectural§Everything before the first census is conjectural.§第一次人口普查之前的一切都是**推测**。
conjecture§I conjecture that the second hand belongs to his son.§我**推测**第二种笔迹是他儿子的。
conjoin§Two ideas conjoined badly can look like one bad idea.§两个想法**拼接**不当，看上去就像一个糟糕的想法。
connoisseur§You need not be a connoisseur to notice the repair.§不必是**鉴赏家**也能看出那处修补。
conscientious§A conscientious objector, he served in the ambulance corps.§作为**出于良心**的拒服兵役者，他在救护队服役。
conscript§Conscripts built the road and were never named on it.§这条路是**应征士兵**修的，路上从未刻下他们的名字。
consecrate§The ground was consecrated before a single stone was laid.§一块石头还没砌，这块地就已被**祝圣**。
consecration§Consecration of the site took a morning; building it took nine years.§场地**祝圣**用了一个上午，建造用了九年。
consequential§A consequential silence followed the question.§问题之后是一阵**意味深长**的沉默。
conservatism§Conservatism in method allows boldness in conclusion.§方法上的**保守**使结论上的大胆成为可能。
conserve§Conserve your energy for the last two miles.§把体力**留到**最后两英里。
considerable§A considerable part of the collection has never been photographed.§这批藏品中有**相当**一部分从未被拍照。
consign§Two of the three drafts were consigned to the fire.§三份草稿中有两份被**投进了火里**。
consistency§The consistency of the batter matters more than the recipe.§面糊的**稠度**比配方更重要。
console§A console table stood between the two windows.§两扇窗之间摆着一张**条案**。
consolidate§Consolidate the notes before the details go cold.§趁细节还没变冷，先把笔记**整理起来**。
consonance§The vowel consonance carries the line more than the rhyme does.§承载这一行的与其说是韵脚，不如说是元音的**和谐**。
consort§The queen's consort never appears in the official portraits.§女王的**配偶**从未出现在官方肖像中。
conspicuous§He made a conspicuous show of checking his watch.§他很**显眼**地做出看表的样子。
conspirator§Fellow conspirators rarely make good witnesses.§**同谋者**很少能当好证人。
constellation§A constellation is a line of sight, not a group of neighbors.§**星座**是视线上的排列，不是邻近的一群星。
consternation§To the consternation of the organizers, nobody came.§令组织者**惊愕**的是，一个人也没来。
constitute§What constitutes evidence here is not settled.§在这里什么**算作**证据尚无定论。
constrain§Fear of error constrains a young researcher more than any rule.§对出错的恐惧比任何规定都更**束缚**年轻研究者。
constructive§The comment was constructive and nobody acted on it.§这条意见很有**建设性**，却没人采纳。
consultation§Consultation with two engineers changed the whole approach.§与两位工程师的**咨询**改变了整个方案。
consummate§The deal was consummated at a table borrowed from a café.§这笔交易是在一张从咖啡馆借来的桌子上**敲定**的。
consumption§Domestic consumption fell while exports rose.§国内**消费**下降，出口却上升。
contagious§Panic is more contagious than any illness on a ship.§在船上，恐慌比任何疾病都更具**传染性**。
contemplative§A contemplative order kept the library for six centuries.§一个**沉思**修会守护这座图书馆达六个世纪。
contemptible§There is nothing contemptible about changing your mind.§改变主意没有什么**可鄙**的。
